title: Mosaic CDKL5 deficiency drives progressive inhibitory circuit remodelling
title_zh: 嵌合型CDKL5缺乏驱动抑制性神经回路的进行性重塑
abstract: Abstract CDKL5 deficiency disorder predominantly affects heterozygous females, in whom random X-chromosome inactivation generates cellular CDKL5 mosaicism. Although mosaicism is a defining feature of the disease, whether it actively drives disease progression or simply reflects the genetic mode of inheritance remains unknown. Here, we combined age-comparative electrophysiology, quantitative synaptic imaging, transcriptomic profiling and postmortem human brain analyses to determine how mosaic CDKL5 deficiency shapes inhibitory circuit remodeling during disease progression. Heterozygous Cdkl5 female mice exhibited striking age- and region-specific remodeling of inhibitory neurotransmission. Hippocampal inhibition was initially enhanced but progressively declined with age, whereas cortical inhibitory transmission remained preserved at 3 months and increased in middle-aged animals. These functional changes were accompanied by dynamic remodeling of inhibitory presynaptic terminals, persistent disruption of inhibitory synapse organization and reduced hippocampal gephyrin-positive puncta despite preservation of the major inhibitory interneuron populations. At 12 months, heterozygous females also exhibited a higher density of IBA1/CD68 double-positive microglia in both regions compared with age-matched wild-type controls. Importantly, complete Cdkl5 deficiency failed to reproduce the progressive loss of inhibitory presynaptic terminals observed in heterozygous females, indicating that this phenotype is specific to the mosaic condition rather than a simple consequence of complete Cdkl5 loss. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a temporal transition from alterations detected at 3 months in immune–synaptic regulatory pathways to activity-dependent transcriptional programs associated with reduced structural and homeostatic support, consistent with progressive hippocampal circuit reorganization. Exploratory analyses of postmortem cortical tissue from individuals with CDD revealed differences in inhibitory presynaptic labeling between the available young and adult cases, suggesting that inhibitory alterations may also vary with age in human CDD. Together, these findings identify mosaic CDKL5 deficiency as a biologically distinct circuit state characterized by progressive, region-specific inhibitory circuit remodeling and provide a mechanistic framework for disease progression in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
abstract_zh: 摘要 CDKL5缺乏障碍主要影响杂合性女性，其中随机X染色体失活产生细胞水平的CDKL5嵌合。尽管嵌合性是该疾病的定义性特征，但它是否积极驱动疾病进展，还是仅反映遗传方式的表现，尚不清楚。在此，我们结合年龄对比电生理学、定量突触成像、转录组分析以及人死后脑组织研究，以确定嵌合型CDKL5缺乏如何在疾病进程中塑造抑制性回路重塑。杂合性Cdkl5雌性小鼠表现出抑制性神经传递显著的年龄和区域特异性重塑。海马抑制最初增强，但随年龄增长而逐渐下降，而皮层抑制性传递在3个月时保持稳定，并在中年动物中增加。这些功能变化伴随着抑制性前突触终端的动态重塑、抑制性突触组织的持续破坏以及海马gephyrin阳性斑点数量减少，尽管主要抑制性中间神经元群体得以保留。12个月时，杂合性雌性两个脑区的IBA1/CD68双阳性小胶质细胞密度也高于年龄匹配的野生型对照。重要的是，完全Cdkl5缺乏未能复制在杂合性雌性中观察到的抑制性前突触终端进行性丢失，表明该表型特异于嵌合状态，而非简单由完全Cdkl5缺失所致。转录组分析揭示了从3个月时检测到的免疫-突触调节通路改变，向与结构和稳态支持减少相关的活动依赖性转录程序的时间转变，符合海马回路的进行性重组。对CDD个体死后皮层组织的探索性分析显示，可用的年轻和成人病例之间抑制性前突触标记存在差异，提示人类CDD中的抑制性改变也可能随年龄而变化。这些发现共同确定嵌合型CDKL5缺乏为一种独特的回路状态，其特征是进行性的区域特异性抑制性回路重塑，并为CDKL5缺乏障碍的疾病进展提供了机制框架。
